gloss: total stranger; unknown person; someone never met before

definitions.gloss: total stranger; unknown person; someone one has never seen or met
definitions.explanation: A person one has never seen ({見|み}ず) and does not know ({知|し}らず). Emphasizes the complete lack of prior acquaintance.

examples.japanese: {見|み}ず{知|し}らずの{人|ひと}に{話|はな}しかけられた。
examples.english: I was spoken to by a total stranger.

examples.japanese: {見|み}ず{知|し}らずの{土地|とち}で{迷|まよ}ってしまった。
examples.english: I got lost in an unfamiliar place.

examples.japanese: {見|み}ず{知|し}らずの{人|ひと}を{簡単|かんたん}に{信用|しんよう}してはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't easily trust people you don't know.

notes:
STRUCTURE:
{見|み}ず (not having seen - negative form of {見|み}る)
+ {知|し}らず (not knowing - negative form of {知|し}る)

The classical negative suffix ず creates a formal/literary compound.

GRAMMAR:
・{見|み}ず{知|し}らずの + noun (as no-adjective)
・{見|み}ず{知|し}らずの{人|ひと} - a person one doesn't know
・{見|み}ず{知|し}らずの{土地|とち} - unfamiliar land

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{見|み}ず{知|し}らずの{人|ひと} - total stranger (person)
・{見|み}ず{知|し}らずの{土地|とち}/{場所|ばしょ} - unfamiliar place
・{見|み}ず{知|し}らずの{他人|たにん} - complete stranger

NUANCE:
Can modify both people and places, unlike {赤|あか}の{他人|たにん} which only refers to people.

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・{赤|あか}の{他人|たにん} - complete stranger (emphasizes no relationship)
・{知|し}らない{人|ひと} - unknown person (simpler)
・{行|ゆ}きずり - passerby, chance encounter
・{初|はじ}めて{会|あ}う{人|ひと} - person meeting for the first time

REGISTER:
Slightly literary due to classical negative form ず. Natural in both spoken and written Japanese.
